summary:
Setting foot on Mars shouldn't mean walking into the unknown. We developed MARSBOUND, an interactive first-person Marswalk simulation paired with a multi-layered Tactical GIS navigation system designed for the first human explorers of Jezero Crater.

To solve the challenge, MARSBOUND synthesizes decades of open NASA data into one unified, field-ready survival map. We integrated high-resolution MRO HiRISE surface imagery, MOLA topographic contours, CRISM hyperspectral mineralogy, and Perseverance’s RIMFAX subsurface radar echograms. Explorers can plan safe traverses across steep delta scarps, navigate low-gravity terrain (0.38g) with real-time solar atmospheric scattering, monitor vital life-support telemetry (O2 consumption and suit power), and investigate authentic rock outcrops using handheld Raman spectrometry and core drilling.

Robotic missions laid the groundwork; humans will take the next steps. MARSBOUND transforms complex satellite datasets into an intuitive, life-saving guide—empowering future astronauts to explore safely and conduct high-yield planetary science on the Martian frontier.
details:
The Inspiration & Concept

When our team sat down to tackle the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, we asked ourselves a simple question: If human astronauts set foot on Mars tomorrow, what would their dashboard actually look like?

Robotic rovers and orbiters have gathered extraordinary troves of Martian data over the last three decades, but that data lives in siloed archives, planetary databases, and static research papers. On Mars, 140 million miles from Earth, with radio signals taking up to 24 minutes for a round-trip, an astronaut standing at the edge of Jezero Crater cannot wait for mission control. They need immediate, real-time, life-or-death spatial awareness.

We built MARSBOUND to transform static orbital science into an intuitive, living survival companion for human Marswalks.

MARSBOUND is a zero-install, browser-based 3D exploration and tactical GIS platform designed as an operational survival and mapping companion for humanity's first crewed Marswalks. Built for the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge, MARSBOUND bridges over twenty years of NASA robotic planetary science into an interactive, synchronized dual-view dashboard: a boots-on-the-ground 0.38g EVA simulation paired with an orbital telemetry GIS console centered on Jezero Crater (18.4447∘N, 77.4508∘E).

What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

MARSBOUND is a zero-install, browser-native 3D exploration and tactical GIS platform that drops users into a synchronized dual-view experience:

  1. Boots-on-the-Ground 3D Simulation: An astronaut's first-person Extravehicular Activity (EVA) view of Jezero Crater's ancient lake delta, operating under realistic 0.38g0.38g0.38g Martian gravity, terrain physics, and dynamic solar illumination.
  2. Tactical GIS Console: An interactive geospatial heads-up display synchronizing orbital satellite telemetry directly with surface navigation. Explorers can view live breadcrumb trails, measure real distance vectors with an interactive ruler, set objective waypoints, and monitor life-support telemetry (oxygen draw rate, suit battery power, and heart rate).
    • MRO HiRISE: High-resolution visible light surface orthomosaics for boulder recognition and terrain roughness.
    • MGS MOLA: Laser altimeter digital elevation models with contour lines and hazardous slope warnings.
    • MRO CRISM: Hyperspectral mineralogy mapping ancient lacustrine clays, carbonates, and olivine.
    • Mars 2020 RIMFAX: Subsurface ground-penetrating radar echograms revealing stratified layers down to 10 meters beneath the Martian regolith.
  3. Surface Operations & Field Laboratory: Explorers can traverse steep terrain on foot or pilot a pressurized rover at 60–80 km/h with responsive Ackermann steering. At 25 georeferenced NASA sample cache sites, users deploy drill tools and examine cores in an onboard laboratory equipped with simulated PIXL (X-ray fluorescence) and CheMin (X-ray diffraction) instruments.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

We grounded every design decision in the real physical constraints of Martian exploration:

  • Human Physiological Limits: Mars offers no breathable air (6.1 hPa, 95% CO2​) and freezing temperatures (−63∘C). Our HUD tracks realistic consumables consumption where running consumes oxygen faster, forcing the explorer to plan safe turnaround margins.
  • Topographical Hazards: The Jezero river delta has vertical scarps and loose scree. We incorporated MOLA-derived slope-hazard alerts so explorers don't drive into steep dead ends.
  • Cognitive Load Under Stress: An astronaut in an EVA suit cannot decipher complex GIS software with tiny menus. We designed high-contrast, glanceable telemetry, color-coded symbology, and intuitive interactive tools.
  • Accessibility & Device Parity: Real field crews use handheld tablets; classroom students use Chromebooks or phones. We built a custom touch-native mobile landscape interface with dual virtual thumbsticks and pinch-to-zoom mapping so anyone can explore without dedicated gaming hardware.

How Is Our Project Creative?

Most mapping tools are either purely 2D top-down maps or disconnected 3D tech demos. MARSBOUND bridges both worlds seamlessly.

We created an editorial-grade narrative framework styled like an authentic expedition dossier—connecting historical robotic discoveries with future human footsteps. By overlaying real RIMFAX radar radargrams alongside 3D surface boulders and CRISM mineral signatures, users don't just see a terrain map; they understand why Perseverance stopped at Octavia E. Butler Landing or Skinner Cove, and what it feels like to conduct fieldwork at those exact coordinates.

Tools, Languages, & Technologies Used

  • Frontend & UI: React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Canvas API.
  • 3D Graphics & Physics: Three.js (WebGL), custom procedural shaders for atmospheric dust scattering, low-gravity kinematic controllers, and responsive vehicle physics.
    • NASA MRO HiRISE (High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment) Jezero DTM and mosaic tiles.
    • NASA MGS MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter) topographic elevations.
    • NASA MRO CRISM (Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars) mineralogy data.
    • NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover RIMFAX (Radar Imager for Mars' Subsurface Experiment) radargrams and official published sample cache dossiers.
  • Audio & Spatial Ambience: Web Audio API synthesizing Martian wind resonance and suit biometrics.

Intended Impact

MARSBOUND has a dual horizon:

  • For Space Exploration: It serves as a proof-of-concept for how NASA's Artemis Moon-to-Mars missions can package multi-instrument orbital telemetry into lightweight, astronaut-operable tactical HUDs that function completely offline on local compute nodes.
  • For Global STEM Education: Millions of students around the world know that Perseverance is on Mars, but very few have interacted with its raw scientific data. MARSBOUND democratizes planetary science, turning complex PDS (Planetary Data System) archives into an exciting, accessible expedition that sparks the next generation of planetary scientists and astronauts.
